research_question: What is the causal effect of job training programs on employment outcomes for displaced workers?
background: Job training programs are commonly used policy interventions to help unemployed workers gain new skills and find employment. However, selection into these programs is often non-random, with more motivated or skilled workers more likely to participate. This framing addresses the causal question of whether these programs actually improve employment outcomes.

variables.name: job_training
variables.description: Participation in job training program (1 = participated, 0 = did not participate)

variables.name: employment_status
variables.description: Employment status 6 months after program completion (1 = employed, 0 = unemployed)

variables.name: earnings
variables.description: Monthly earnings 6 months after program completion

variables.name: age
variables.description: Age of the worker in years

variables.name: prior_experience
variables.description: Years of work experience in previous field

variables.name: unemployment_duration
variables.description: Duration of unemployment in months before program

variables.name: local_unemployment_rate
variables.description: Local unemployment rate at time of program entry

variables.name: program_assignment
variables.description: Random assignment to job training program eligibility (1 = eligible, 0 = not eligible)

estimand.description: Local average treatment effect for compliers (those who participate when eligible but not when ineligible)
estimand.target_population: Displaced workers who would participate in job training if made eligible but would not participate if ineligible

study_design.description: Instrumental variables design using randomized program eligibility as instrument for actual participation
study_design.assignment_mechanism: Randomized eligibility determination with voluntary participation
study_design.data_collection_method: Administrative program records combined with employment outcome data

assumptions.name: Instrument Relevance
assumptions.description: Program eligibility strongly affects actual participation in job training
assumptions.rationale: Weak instruments produce biased and inconsistent LATE estimates

assumptions.name: Instrument Exclusion
assumptions.description: Program eligibility affects employment outcomes only through actual participation in training
assumptions.test_method: Overidentification tests if multiple instruments available
assumptions.rationale: Core IV assumption ensuring instrument affects outcome only through treatment

assumptions.name: Independence
assumptions.description: Randomized eligibility is independent of potential outcomes and participation decisions
assumptions.test_method: Balance tests on baseline covariates across eligibility groups

assumptions.name: Monotonicity
assumptions.description: No defiers - no workers who would participate only when ineligible
assumptions.rationale: Ensures LATE interpretation as effect for compliers

assumptions.name: Stable Unit Treatment Value
assumptions.description: One worker's participation does not affect another's employment outcome

validation_criteria.name: First Stage Strength
validation_criteria.description: F-statistic from first-stage regression should exceed conventional threshold

validation_criteria.name: Randomization Balance
validation_criteria.description: Baseline covariates should be balanced across eligibility groups

validation_criteria.name: Exclusion Restriction Test
validation_criteria.description: Test for direct effects of eligibility on outcomes

data_requirements.data_structure: Individual-level panel data with baseline and follow-up observations

limitations: LATE only identifies effect for compliers, not all workers
Results may not generalize to other job training programs or populations
Potential for spillover effects if labor market is tight
Measurement error in employment outcomes could bias estimates
Long-term effects beyond 6 months are not captured
